documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M here to set up primary care. Has not had regular primary care for a while; his ID clinic wanted him to have a PCP for everything else.

CC: getting weaker, and food sticks.

HPI: Over the last several months he has noticed his arms and legs giving out on him. Hard to get up off the floor, carrying drywall was the first thing to go and he hasn't worked construction since he went out on disability. No falls yet. Separately, trouble getting food and sometimes drinks to go down; he eats slowly and drinks a lot of water with meals. He wonders if the two are connected because his brother has a muscle disease that started with leg weakness.

PMH: HIV, told he has AIDS because of repeated bacterial pneumonias years ago at the old practice. Followed at an outside ID clinic, on bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily, says he doesn't miss doses. Recurrent bacterial pneumonia in the past. Former IV drug use, in remission for years, not interested in going into detail today and I didn't push.
Meds: B/F/TAF daily (ID prescribes). Acetaminophen 500 mg q6h prn aches.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
FH: brother with progressive limb-girdle weakness, told it is genetic. Father COPD. Paternal uncle lung cancer at 62.
SH: smokes 1.5 packs/day since age 20, about 35 pack-years. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. On disability from construction.

ROS: no fever, no chest pain. Denies weight loss. No rash.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Pleasant, in no distress. Oropharynx clear. Lungs clear bilaterally. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft. Has to push off his thighs to stand from the chair. Reflexes present and symmetric. Skin without lesions.

A/P:
1. Progressive limb weakness + dysphagia, family history of a genetic myopathy. Neurology referral placed; likely needs neuromuscular workup.
2. HIV/AIDS - per ID. Requesting their last note and labs.
3. Tobacco use disorder - wants to try something. Nicotine patch 21 mg daily sent. Talked about cutting down while on it. Not setting a quit date yet.
4. Hx IVDU in remission. HCV antibody today.
5. Baseline CBC, CMP.
6. Records request to prior practice.
RTC 3-4 months, sooner once neuro weighs in.

OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC
Visit date: 05/20/2021

45-year-old man with HIV, AIDS-defining history of recurrent bacterial pneumonia, here for routine follow-up. Taking bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide daily, reports full adherence, no side effects. No recent infections.

Allergies: penicillin (rash).
Social: active smoker, about 1.5 ppd. Prior IVDU, in sustained remission.

Labs today: CD4 342 cells/uL. HIV-1 RNA not detected (<20 copies/mL).

Assessment: virologically suppressed on current regimen. CD4 above 200, no OI prophylaxis indicated.
Plan: continue B/F/TAF, 90-day supply sent. Return in about 1 year with labs, sooner as needed. Encouraged smoking cessation. Patient states he is establishing with a new PCP; copy of this note to be sent.

conditions.label: Hereditary myopathy with chaperone protein abnormality

reports.text:
Specimen: skeletal muscle, left quadriceps, open biopsy.
Gross: received in multiple portions, fresh and in fixative.
Microscopic: skeletal muscle with myopathic changes. Immunohistochemistry demonstrates abnormal accumulation of chaperone proteins within muscle fibers. No inflammatory infiltrate. No vasculitis.
Comment: findings support a hereditary myopathy involving chaperone protein abnormality. Correlate with genetic evaluation.
reports.conclusion: Skeletal muscle with abnormal chaperone protein accumulation, consistent with a hereditary myopathy.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC
Date of service: 08/16/2021
Reason for referral: weakness, swallowing difficulty

Thank you for sending Mr. Jacobs, a 45-year-old right-handed man with HIV, seen first in July for slowly worsening weakness of the arms and legs over many months. He also has trouble swallowing. His brother has a progressive limb-girdle pattern of weakness attributed to a genetic myopathy.

We obtained a left quadriceps muscle biopsy on 07/27/2021. Today we reviewed the result with him: abnormal accumulation of chaperone proteins within the muscle fibers, no inflammation.

Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily, acetaminophen as needed, nicotine patch.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
Social: smoker, 35 pack-years. Rare alcohol. On medical disability from construction work.
Family: brother with genetic myopathy, as above.

Impression: hereditary myopathy with chaperone protein abnormality. The family history fits an inherited process. Genetic counseling offered; he will think about it.

Regarding the dysphagia: he describes both solids and liquids hanging up. That pattern is not typical for a myopathic oropharyngeal problem, and I would recommend gastroenterology evaluation for an esophageal cause.

Plan: home exercise program, avoid exhausting effort. Return in 1 year, sooner if breathing or swallowing change. Will monitor respiratory function at follow-up.

Neurology

documents.title: Neurology results discussed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Went over the neuromuscular letter: biopsy shows an inherited myopathy, same family of problem as his brother. He was not surprised. Neuro wants GI to look at the swallowing, which makes sense to me - solids and liquids both. GI referral placed. He will keep up the home exercises. Asked how the patch is going: wearing it most days, down to about a pack a day on a good day.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY ASSOCIATES
Date of service: 12/14/2021
Referring: primary care

Mr. Jacobs returns to go over his swallowing workup. He has HIV, a hereditary myopathy diagnosed by neurology this summer, and has been seen once here already. For several months food and liquids alike hang up behind the breastbone. He brings back undigested food, sometimes his breath smells bad, and he gets a vague, mild chest discomfort with meals. No weight loss, no pain with swallowing, no heartburn.

Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, acetaminophen prn, nicotine patch.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
Social: current smoker, 35 pack-years. Alcohol 1-2 drinks monthly. On medical disability.
Family: brother with a genetic myopathy; father COPD.

Vitals: T 36.9 C, BP 126/78, HR 74, RR 14.
Exam: unremarkable.

Studies since the first visit:
- Barium esophagram: dilated esophagus with retained contrast and smooth tapering to a narrow segment at the gastroesophageal junction (bird's-beak appearance).
- Upper endoscopy 11/30/2021: retained food in a dilated esophagus. No mass and no stricture at the GE junction; the scope passed with gentle pressure. GE junction biopsies benign.
- High-resolution esophageal manometry: absent peristalsis with incomplete relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter.

Impression: achalasia. Endoscopy does not suggest a mechanical or malignant cause.

Plan: we discussed options. Starting nifedipine extended-release 30 mg daily. Eat upright, small bites, liquids with meals, stay upright after eating. Return in 6 months.

Gastroenterology

OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC
Date of service: 08/23/2022

One-year follow-up for hereditary myopathy with chaperone protein abnormality. He feels the weakness has progressed slowly; stairs and getting up from low seats are harder than last year. No shortness of breath, no orthopnea. Swallowing now attributed to achalasia by GI, on nifedipine.

He has been thinking about lung cancer - father has COPD, uncle had lung cancer, he knows he smokes too much. Wants to know if there's a test.

Explained what the scan is, the false-positive and follow-up scan issue, and that quitting does more than any scan. Added to problem list so we catch it at 50. He liked having a plan.
- Tobacco - same; patch refilled.
- Achalasia - nifedipine ER 30, GI following.
- Myopathy - neuro yearly.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Came in because of purple spots. For several weeks he has had dark purple spots on the roof of his mouth and on both lower legs. Not painful. Also a dry cough that won't quit, several weeks, no blood. Waking up soaked at night. Pants are loose - down about 7 kg since last year on our scale. No fever he knows of. Still taking his HIV pill every day.

O: Vitals as charted; weight 71.0 kg (78 last spring). Thin. Several violaceous macules and papules on the hard palate. Multiple similar purple papules on both shins and calves, non-blanching. No adenopathy felt in the neck or axillae. Lungs: clear to auscultation, no crackles. Heart regular. Abdomen soft.

A/P: violaceous skin and palate lesions with cough, night sweats and weight loss in a man with AIDS. Kaposi sarcoma is high on the list; infection needs to be excluded too.
- Urgent dermatology referral for biopsy - called and got him in on 2/19.
- CT chest ordered.
- CBC, CMP today.
- Messaged his ID clinic, they will move his visit up.
- Return precautions for fever or shortness of breath.
I'll call with results.

documents.title: ID clinic notified
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called ID clinic nurse line per PCP, relayed lesions, cough, weight loss, night sweats. They will see pt 2/27 with labs and want derm and CT results faxed.

reports.text:
OUTSIDE IMAGING CENTER
CT chest without contrast.
Indication: chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats; HIV.
Comparison: none.

Findings: Bilateral perihilar infiltrates. Small bilateral pleural effusions. No pneumothorax. Central airways patent. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal mass. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. Bones without suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral perihilar infiltrates with small bilateral pleural effusions.

events.reason: Violaceous lesions of hard palate and lower extremities

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, left lower leg, 4 mm punch biopsy.
Microscopic: dermal proliferation of spindle-shaped cells forming slit-like vascular spaces, with neovascularization and extravasated red blood cells.
Comment: diagnostic of Kaposi sarcoma in this clinical setting.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY
Date of service: 02/19/2024
Referred urgently by PCP.

48-year-old man with HIV on ART and achalasia, seen for purple lesions of the palate and legs. He also has a dry cough lasting weeks, with weight loss and drenching night sweats over the same period.

Allergies: penicillin (rash).
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, nifedipine ER 30 mg, acetaminophen prn, nicotine patch.

Exam: numerous red-violet papules that do not blanch, on the hard palate and over both lower legs.
Chest CT from 02/13 reviewed: bilateral perihilar infiltrates, small effusions.

Procedure: 4 mm punch biopsy, left lower leg, after consent; hemostasis with pressure, one suture.

Pathology (02/22): spindle cell proliferation with new vessel formation and red cells outside the vessels - Kaposi sarcoma.

Assessment: Kaposi sarcoma involving skin and oral mucosa; the chest CT raises concern for lung involvement.
Plan: urgent oncology referral placed; ID aware. Suture out in 10 to 14 days at PCP or here.

Dermatology

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC
Visit date: 02/27/2024

Seen sooner than planned for biopsy-proven Kaposi sarcoma of skin and palate, with perihilar infiltrates and small effusions on CT, cough, night sweats and weight loss.

Adherent to bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF.
CD4 291 cells/uL. HIV-1 RNA not detected (<20 copies/mL).

Assessment: KS despite viral suppression. Infection must be excluded as a cause of the lung findings before they are attributed to KS. Pulmonary referral for bronchoscopy with BAL arranged; oncology referral already placed by dermatology. CD4 above 200: no PJP prophylaxis.
Plan: continue ART unchanged through chemotherapy, no interactions of concern with liposomal doxorubicin. Labs again in 6 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Suture removal

documents.body: Single suture removed from left lower leg biopsy site. Site clean and healed, no drainage. Pt has bronchoscopy next week and oncology the week after.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy with Bronchoalveolar Lavage
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY - BRONCHOSCOPY REPORT
Date of procedure: 03/07/2024
Indication: bilateral perihilar infiltrates and small effusions in a man with HIV and newly diagnosed cutaneous/oral Kaposi sarcoma; exclude infection.
Allergies: penicillin.
Sedation: moderate, monitored.

Findings: vocal cords normal. Trachea and main bronchi patent. Airway mucosa without focal lesion. Scant clear secretions.
BAL right middle lobe, returns clear.

BAL results (final 03/13): bacterial culture no growth. AFB smear negative; AFB culture no growth so far, final at 6 weeks. Pneumocystis stain negative.

Impression: no infection identified on BAL. Results to oncology and ID.
No complications; discharged home same day.

Pulmonology

documents.title: Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY
Date of service: 03/12/2024

Reason: Kaposi sarcoma, referred by dermatology.

History: HIV on ART with suppressed viral load, CD4 291 last month. Several weeks of red-violet lesions on the palate and lower legs, punch biopsy 02/19 Kaposi sarcoma. Dry cough, night sweats, weight loss of about 7 kg. CT chest 02/13: bilateral perihilar infiltrates with small pleural effusions. Bronchoscopy 03/07 with BAL negative for bacteria, AFB and Pneumocystis.
Other history: hereditary myopathy, achalasia on nifedipine ER, tobacco use (35 pack-years, current), remote IVDU in remission.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).

Exam: palate and bilateral lower-leg violaceous papules as described. Lungs clear. No hepatosplenomegaly.

Assessment: AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma involving skin and oral mucosa, with pulmonary involvement - with infection excluded, the perihilar infiltrates and effusions are attributed to KS. Systemic therapy indicated.

Plan: liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks, 6 cycles, starting 03/18/2024. Continue ART per ID. CBC before each cycle here. Restaging CT chest after cycle 6. Discussed hair, mouth sores, low counts, hand-foot reaction, infusion reactions.

Oncology

documents.body:
Here after finishing 6 cycles of liposomal doxorubicin (last 7/1). Oncology note and restaging CT in chart: lung infiltrates and effusions gone. Lesions faded. He feels like himself again - eating better within the limits of the achalasia, no cough, no sweats.

Weight up about 3.5 kg since March.

Exam: palate with faint flat purplish discoloration only. Shins with flat brown-violet macules, no raised lesions. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
- Kaposi sarcoma - treatment complete, good response. Oncology surveillance every 6 months.
- HIV - ID visit in October.
- Achalasia, myopathy - unchanged.
- Tobacco - 1 ppd. Again offered help; he'll stay on the patch.
- CBC, CMP today after chemo.
- FIT overdue (due June) - kit given.
Flu/COVID in October. Check in late fall.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood counts have recovered nicely after chemo and your kidney and liver tests are normal.

documents.body: Flu (trivalent) 0.5 mL IM L deltoid and 2024-25 COVID 0.3 mL IM R deltoid given. Tolerated. Reminded pt about the FIT kit, he says it is still on the counter.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home, ID verified by name and DOB.

Short check-in. ID note from October in chart: viral load undetectable, CD4 318. No new skin spots he can see, the old ones keep fading. No cough. Swallowing the same on nifedipine ER - slow meals, sleeps propped up. Legs about the same; uses acetaminophen now and then.
Still smoking around a pack a day. Needs patches.

Exam limited to video: comfortable, speaking full sentences, no visible lesions on the face or lips.

A/P:
- Kaposi sarcoma s/p liposomal doxorubicin - oncology surveillance due February.
- HIV - ID every 6 months.
- Achalasia - GI, nifedipine.
- Hereditary myopathy - stable by report; reminded him to rebook neurology.
- Tobacco - patch refilled.
- Turns 50 in December 2025 - lung screening CT then.
- FIT still not returned; he'll mail it.
Office visit in the spring.

events.reason: Rash on legs and joint stiffness after antibiotic course

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, right lower leg, 4 mm punch biopsy.
Microscopic: perivascular infiltrate of neutrophils with nuclear dust (leukocytoclasis) and fibrinoid necrosis of the walls of small dermal vessels. No spindle cell proliferation.
Comment: leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis; correlate clinically.
reports.conclusion: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis of small dermal vessels.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of visit: 02/02/2026

CC: leg rash, stiff joints.

HPI: 50M with HIV on ART and a history of Kaposi sarcoma treated with chemotherapy in 2024. About a week ago a rash came up on both legs and has spread and darkened since. Achy, stiff joints and tired. Seen at an urgent care 01/19 for pneumonia and given sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim DS twice daily for 10 days, finished 01/28. He says his lips swelled for an afternoon during the course and went down on their own. No fever. No weight loss. No belly pain.

PMH: HIV/AIDS, Kaposi sarcoma, achalasia, hereditary myopathy, tobacco use, remote IVDU, recurrent pneumonia.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, nifedipine ER 30 mg, nicotine patch, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
Social: smokes about a pack a day.

Exam: vitals reviewed, afebrile. Both lower legs with many non-blanching purpuric papules, palpable, no ulceration. Lips and tongue normal now. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender. Joints without effusion.

Labs: platelets normal. PT/INR normal. UA without blood or protein.

Dermatology consulted by phone, came down and did a 4 mm punch biopsy of the right leg.

Assessment: palpable purpura after sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim - drug-induced urticarial vasculitis most likely; biopsy pending.
Disposition: home. Antibiotic already finished. Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim added as an allergy (urticarial vasculitis and angioedema). Acetaminophen for joint stiffness. Dermatology clinic follow-up in about 1 month; return for fever, spreading rash, abdominal pain, dark urine, swelling of lips or throat.

Addendum 02/05: biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis of small dermal vessels, consistent with the clinical diagnosis. Patient informed by phone.

documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, Todd - glad it's fading. Avoid that antibiotic from here on. We'll get the ER records. If the rash comes back, you get a fever, or your belly or joints get worse, get seen. We still need to get you in for a visit; call the front desk when you can.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY
Date of service: 03/09/2026

Follow-up after the ED visit of 02/02 for palpable purpura on both legs following a course of sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. The rash cleared over about two weeks after the antibiotic ended; joint stiffness gone. No new lesions.

Biopsy reviewed with him: leukocytoclastic vasculitis of small dermal vessels.

Exam: legs without purpura. Old flat macules from prior Kaposi sarcoma, unchanged. No new violaceous lesions.

Assessment: drug-induced urticarial vasculitis from sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, resolved. Avoid sulfonamide antibiotics. No further treatment needed.
Return as needed.

Dermatology
